newsitem.title: USA: America West Airlines to take 3Q charge.
newsitem.headline: America West Airlines to take 3Q charge.

text.p: America West Airlines Inc said on Thursday that it will take a non-cash, non-recurring pretax charge of $65 million in the third quarter of 1996.

The charge is primarily the result of the airline's agreement in principle to acquire up to 34 new aircraft from Airbus Industrie. This new order, announced on Wednesday, replaces an order for 24 aircraft that was entered into in 1990.
America West expects to release its third quarter results on Oct. 25.

"The new arrangements offer improved financial terms and conditions and a mix of aircraft types better suited to the company's requirements," said W. A. Franke, America West's chairman, president and chief executive officer.

In addition, America West announced it will file a registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission covering the refinancing of eight to 12 Airbus A320 aircraft currently operated by the airline pursuant to leases with U.S. affiliates of GPA Group plc, the Irish aircraft lessor.

This refinancing, which is expected to close in late November 1996, will lower America West's leasing costs between $7 million to $12 million over the 15 year life of the leases depending on the number of aircraft financed, the company said.
America West, the nation's ninth largest airline, provides service to more than 90 destinations in the U.S., Canada and Mexico.
